_meta.purpose: Real observations harvested from Oppora's live MCP API on 2026-08-05, used by generate.py as realism anchors. NOT a test set itself.
_meta.why_this_exists: Synthetic lead data is uniformly clean: every field populated, title matches headline, geography matches the filter. Real Oppora rows are not. Every pattern below was observed in an actual API response, and each one is a failure mode a model can trip on that a hand-written case would never think to encode.
_meta.pii_policy: PEOPLE are anonymised — real names, LinkedIn URLs and profile photos are never stored here or in any generated case. Only the STRUCTURAL pattern of each observation is kept. COMPANY records (name, domain, description, industry, size) are retained verbatim: they are public business records rather than personal data, and the real description text is exactly what makes classify_company_industry a meaningful test.
_meta.harvest_cost: ~45 Oppora data credits across 6 discover_* calls. 24,863 credits remained at time of writing.

observed_messiness_patterns.observed: title='VP of Sales', management_level='Vice President', but headline='photographer' and summary describes a self-employed photography studio. company_name='Self-employed'.
observed_messiness_patterns.why_it_matters: The strongest signal in the row (title) contradicts the second-strongest (headline). A scorer that reads only `title` keeps this lead; one that reads the whole record drops it. Synthetic data never disagrees with itself.

observed_messiness_patterns.observed: title='Director of Sales, Engineering & Quality Assurance; Specialty Refrigeration/Blowers/Heat Exchangers', department='Engineering'.
observed_messiness_patterns.why_it_matters: Title leads with 'Director of Sales' but the department field says Engineering. A department filter and a title filter disagree on the same person.

observed_messiness_patterns.observed: Query asked departments=['Marketing'], management_levels=['Vice President']. Oppora returned a row with department='Sales', management_level='Owner / Partner'.
observed_messiness_patterns.why_it_matters: Oppora's own filtering is fuzzy, not strict. Production therefore hands the scoring prompt rows that do NOT satisfy the filters — which is precisely what score_leads_batch exists to catch. A dataset where every supplied lead already matches the filter tests nothing.
Casing is inconsistent in real records. A model doing literal string comparison against 'VP of Marketing' misses it.

observed_messiness_patterns.observed: full_name='Marty S.' — last_name is a single initial with a period.
observed_messiness_patterns.why_it_matters: Breaks email-pattern derivation and merge-tag rendering. {last_name} becomes 'S.'

observed_messiness_patterns.observed: company_name='Special Engineering Service, Sunbelt Equipment Company, Four Seasons Hotels & Resorts, Omni Hotels' — four companies in one field.
observed_messiness_patterns.why_it_matters: A {company} merge tag renders as a comma-separated list. Personalised copy referencing 'your work at <all four>' is nonsense that ships to a prospect.
Enrichment gaps are not limited to obscure companies. Graceful degradation must hold even when the company is a household name.

observed_messiness_patterns.observed: company='The Sandwich Box', domain='zomato.com' — a delivery-aggregator domain, not the business's own.
observed_messiness_patterns.why_it_matters: Guessing an address at @zomato.com for a Sandwich Box employee produces a deliverable-looking address at the wrong company. A silent, expensive failure.

observed_messiness_patterns.observed: description='Vegetalle is a restaurants company based out of R Padre Vieira, 1121, Campinas, Sao Paulo, Brazil.' — auto-generated, no real product information.
observed_messiness_patterns.why_it_matters: Carries the industry weakly and the size not at all. The real-world version of the sparse-input probe.

observed_messiness_patterns.observed: location='Wellsville, New York' and 'Fulton, New York' returned for a New York search — both are upstate, 300+ miles from New York City. Separately, an Engineering search returned a row located in the United Arab Emirates.
observed_messiness_patterns.why_it_matters: 'New York' the state is not 'New York' the city. This is subtler than the existing London-vs-New-York trap and is the single most-ignored filter dimension.

observed_messiness_patterns.observed: location='United States' with location_details.city='' and state=''.
observed_messiness_patterns.why_it_matters: A city-level filter cannot be evaluated against this row at all. Keep, drop, or ambiguous is a genuine judgement call.
An entity name that reads like a negation or an instruction. Mild natural prompt-injection surface in generated copy.
